summary: Erected in 1923 on the Gila's Glenwood Ranger District as a 35-foot Aermotor LX-24; its log cabin complex was later listed on the National Register.

facts.design: Aermotor LX-24 tower with a 7'x7' wooden cab; the site includes two log cabins and a log shed

events.note: June 1913 Albuquerque Journal item, quoted by Forest Lookouts, refers to a 'Bear Wallows lookout'; unclear whether it was this tower or an earlier structure
Erected on the Glenwood Ranger District; Aermotor LX-24 with 7x7 wooden cab, about 35 feet tall
Wikipedia lead says the cabins and shed were built in 1940 by the Works Progress Administration; its infobox gives 1923 for the same article (disputed)
Silver City Daily Press (April 28, 1967) reports a couple planned to take up their post at the lookout in April 1967
Extensively remodeled: original windows replaced, new stairs installed, roof and exterior walls covered with steel
Cabins and shed complex added to the National Register of Historic Places on January 28, 1988
Bear Fire burned across Bearwallow Mountain and threatened the buildings, per Wikipedia (which cites a Gila National Forest news release)
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register as US 1585, NM 43 on May 22, 2022

corrections.why: The 35 is in feet, not metres: NHLR gives the tower as 35 'beet' high (a typo for feet) and Forest Lookouts says a 35-foot tall tower. 35 ft is about 10.7 m.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR (typo 'beet') and Forest Lookouts (35-foot tall) agree on 35 feet, so the height is recorded as 10.7 m rather than 35 m.

notes_for_editor: Build date for the tower (1923) is consistent across NHLR and Forest Lookouts. The cabins and shed are disputed: the Wikipedia lead says 1940 (WPA), while its infobox says 1923; the NRHP date is 1988. The 1913 'Bear Wallows lookout' reference may indicate an earlier lookout at the site, but no source describes it, so it is recorded only as an 'other' event. The 1967 item is a planned posting from a newspaper, not confirmation that the couple served. The NHLR visit or access status is not stated on the page (access omitted). Not checked: the NRHP nomination on npgallery (not found in search results) and the Wikipedia citation for the 2006 Bear Fire news release. The heritageindex.org NRHP page returned HTTP 403. Staffing is unknown as of 2026.
